body:
When `FastParse` rejects a text, `PersistentZipper.parse_text` falls back to `MarkerParse.of_text`. This covers saved programs with incomplete forms or `¿` markers, and share links. `MarkerParse.of_text` parsed with `Parser.to_zipper`, which inserts the text one character at a time. That's quadratic: each character re-molds and re-grouts the whole sibling sequence it lands in. In a CPU profile, nearly all of its time is `insert` → `remold_regrout` → `remold_exp` / `regrout_affix`.

`Parser.to_segment` already exists for this reason: it splits the input at safe top-level points, "to avoid O(n^2) scaling". This PR makes the load fallback use it.

- `Parser.to_segment_with_manuals` also keeps each piece's projectors. Typing `^^probe(` pins a projector in that piece's refractors, by piece id, and `to_segment` used to throw those away. `to_segment` is now a wrapper, so `splice_paste` is unchanged.
- `Parser.to_zipper_segmented` builds the zipper from the segments, finishing as `to_zipper` does, and restores the projectors.
- `MarkerParse.of_text` uses `to_zipper_segmented`.

Part of #2609, "Performance Challenges (Fall 2026)".

## Measured

Prose alone (the fallback's worst case, one long flat sequence), wall-clock in node, one run per size:

| size | `to_zipper` | segmented |
|---|---|---|
| 1 KB | 0.73 s | 0.16 s |
| 2 KB | 3.28 s | 0.32 s |
| 4 KB | 14.83 s | 0.66 s |
| 8 KB | 64.41 s | 1.30 s |

The segmented column is `to_segment`, which `to_zipper_segmented` wraps, adding one reassembly pass. Over every program in `hazel-programs`, 72 `.hz` files and the tutorials' `@code` and `@test` sections, 128 inputs in all, the fallback takes 63 s in total against 182 s. For example, `b2t2/example-tables.hz` drops from 13.2 s to 2.1 s. One file barely changes: `b2t2/errors-using-tables-browngetacne.hz`, 12.4 s to 12.0 s. It seems to have no safe split points, so it's still one long piece.

## What stays the same, and what doesn't

**On code it's exact.** All 128 inputs print identically both ways with `MarkerParse.to_text`, which prints every hole as `¿`, projectors included.

**On text that isn't code, holes can differ at segment boundaries.** Where one segment ends and the next begins, the final regrout can put a hole on the other side of a space (`String)¿ and` against `to_zipper`'s `String) ¿and`), or add one. On 574 characters of prose it gave 81 holes against 79. The words always come back in order. Code doesn't hit this, because its segments end after complete forms that need no hole between them.

That's accepted here because `to_zipper` isn't stable on such text either: reparsing its own output of the same prose grows it from 732 to 1044 characters.

**Not changed:** paste in the middle of a program still falls back to `to_zipper`. There, pasted text lands inside existing tiles and can complete them, which is why `splice_paste` is guarded to the top level. That's the other path in #2609, left for a separate change.

## Tests

A new group, `Parser.Segmented` (6):
- the four reference programs with projectors (`probes.hz`, `cards.hz`, `tables.hz`, `tuples.hz`) and one without give the same zipper, printed, as `to_zipper`;
- a paragraph of prose gives the same words.

The file cases are `Slow`, about 30 s, since `to_zipper` is what they compare against. The full local suite passes, 4528 tests.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

to_segment_with_manuals keeps each piece's pins, to_segment wraps it for
splice_paste, and to_zipper_segmented builds the zipper, reassembles it
as to_zipper does, and restores the pins. MarkerParse.of_text uses it.

On every program in hazel-programs (128 files and tutorial sections), the

characters of prose); to_zipper is not stable there either, growing its
own output of that prose from 732 to 1044 characters on reparse. Paste in
the middle of a program still uses to_zipper.

A new Parser.Segmented group (6) checks the same zipper on the reference
programs with projectors and one without, and the same words on prose.
The full local suite passes, 4528 tests.
